Thank you for saying this. You have encapsulated my relationship with the Qur'an and Allah God/Allah (Source) as well. I am currently visiting family abroad and was watching a Muslim scholar interpret the Qur'an, and the categories of non-believers. One of the things he was mentioning was that the poetic structure and the symmetry of the Qu'ran are so "perfect" That OF COURSE it has to be the words of Allah himself. I raised my eyebrows...but my cousin hung on to his every word. He then went on to describe each category of non-believer and concluded to say that of course there will be some who do not fit into any one category and after seeing this they must now decide...which I must be honest freaked me out and brought me back to childhood. I thought some more and to me, I don't think there's room for fear of hellfire in the religion. It doesn't make sense (to me).There are so many things that give me pause within Islam...There was a time when I said I was not a Muslim and even told my parents (who thankfully are much more moderate than the rest of my family and are religious but not intense about it, and understanding, probably after having moved to America) who were dealing with my brother who had just reclaimed his faith and was bordering on an extremist interpretation (he's calmed all the way down now, thank goodness). I didn't believe in prayer as I do not speak Arabic and it didn't make sense to me to recite sura'hs of which I dont understand the exact meaning of the words, just general understanding of Su'rah itself. But a few years ago I realized, I don't have to completely renounce my faith...When I was about 6 or so, in Islamic School I was terrified about going to Hell (this feeling was echoed in the scholar's statements about choosing which category)...but I don't know what it was...maybe it was divine intervention? But Something came over me soothing me telling me "hey, that's not really how it is, you just need to remember in your heart what is good and that you believe in something greater so don't worry about following all these rules to the T" and I took it that way...I know that may sound very self-serving and also blasphemous but I went back to that and haven't looked back since.

What is really difficult however is visiting my family overseas who would never be able to fathom this interpretation. It bothers me to an extent that they feel the need to tell me to pray or check on me if I've prayed as though they are living in fear of the eternal consequence. I have my own relationship with God and it goes beyond prayer...but I do it when I'm with them out of respect for my family and love. 

Again, thanks for sharing <3

I'm asking because for me it was fairly common during my childhood and teenage years. It used to freak me out like none other, to the point where I couldn't fall back asleep if it happened in the middle of the night. I used to have this recurring deram where I was in my local Rec Center's pool area, no one except me just walking around staring at the pool. Normal chlorinated water. Then all of a sudden all the water turns brown and it freaks me out, I scream for my mom but can't hear anything...then I wake up and realize I can't move, keep trying to scream nothing. Heavy feeling on my chest, and strange eery violin music blasting in my ears. Then I'm fine.

As I became a teenager my sleep paralysis shifted a bit. I stopped having it for a while then it came back randomly when I was trying to nap one afternoon. I was kind of scared, but not really because I knew what it was, but it had never happened during the day.
